**Retirement at 46 (May 31, 1990)**
- "The pressure wasn't it. It was just too much time" — [PBS Frontline](https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/pages/frontline/shows/betting/pros/lynch.html) [VERIFIED-PRIMARY]
- His father died at 46, and Lynch turned 46 in January 1990. His daughters were 15, 11 and 7. He said he had "two gears, overdrive and park" (Time, April 1990) — [CapexCat](https://capexcat.substack.com/p/peter-lynch-buy-what-you-know)
- "Buy what you know" is a distortion. In 2023 he said "I did not say invest in the stock market." His fuller line is "know what you own" — [Yahoo Finance 2023](https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/news/fidelity-legend-peter-lynch-i-never-said-to-invest-in-the-stock-market-120755736.html); [CapexCat](https://capexcat.substack.com/p/peter-lynch-buy-what-you-know)
- After Lynch, Magellan returned 7.8%/yr from 1990 to mid-2010, 0.4%/yr behind the S&P. Scale ($14B growing to $50B+) eroded the edge — [CBS MoneyWatch](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/lessons-from-a-great-fund-managers-record)

`person:philip-fisher` | confidence: **unverified** | tags: us, process, growth, scuttlebutt, low-turnover

Founded Fisher & Co. in 1931; author of Common Stocks and Uncommon Profits (1958), whose 15 points (sales growth runway, R&D effectiveness, margins, labour relations, management depth and integrity, long-range outlook) and 'scuttlebutt' method (interview customers, suppliers, competitors and ex-employees) shaped Buffett's shift towards quality growth. Signature trade: bought Motorola in 1955 when it was a car-radio maker and held it until his death in 2004 (folklore-grade; held ~5 decades); also Texas Instruments and Dow Chemical. Track record: never audited or published as a fund series - treat any CAGR claim as unverified. Process: very few holdings, held for decades; sell only if the original analysis was wrong, the company no longer meets the 15 points, or a far better opportunity appears - not because the stock looks expensive. Mistakes he described (Developing an Investment Philosophy): early in his career he tried to time the market and bought weak businesses on cheapness; also, never-sell can mean riding a fading leader (Motorola's long decline after the 1990s). Copyable for Indians: scuttlebutt is very doable - dealer checks, distributor calls, LinkedIn hiring trends, product reviews - and is a genuine individual edge in small/mid caps under-covered by analysts.

- **SBC expense:** FY23 $17.9M, FY24 $15.6M, FY25 $34.7M (0.73% of sales, 9.7% of net income, 8.4% of FCF) `[XBRL]`. FY24 was depressed by forfeitures at the CEO exit ("lapping … a non-recurring stock compensation benefit") `[10K25]`. H1 FY26: $15.0M.
- **Overhang:** 400k RSUs + 311k PSUs unvested = **~1.3% of shares**. $35.3M is unrecognised, over 2.0 years `[10K25 n.8]`.
- **"Adjusted" EPS excludes 2024 retention awards** (cash and equity, vesting through Aug-2026): $1.95M of operating income in H1 FY26 and $5.2M in H1 FY25 `[PR-Q2 FY26]`. Small, but it is pay. **We add it back.**
- **Real dilution cost = the buyback cash** needed to hold shares flat. That was ~$270M since 2018 (~$34M a year), roughly equal to SBC plus ESPP. Q2 FY26: 311k shares bought for $60M. A new **$600M authorisation** with no expiry was approved on 29-Aug-2026 `[PR-Q2 FY26]`. Treat SBC as a cash cost: FY25 FCF after SBC = $377M.
